title: SQL Injection - Administrator Login Bypass
impact: Allows an attacker to bypass the login check and potentially gain administrator-level access without valid credentials.
remediation: Use parameterized SQL queries, avoid concatenating user input into SQL statements, and validate inputs on the server.

title: SQL Injection - Unauthorized User Data Exposure
column17: The vulnerable search endpoint can expose user account information, including email addresses and password hashes, without proper authorization.
column18: Use parameterized queries, restrict database account permissions, and prevent user input from being directly inserted into SQL statements.

title: Reflected XSS Through Search Input
impact: A specially crafted search link can cause attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in a visitor's browser.
remediation: Encode untrusted input before rendering it, avoid unsafe HTML insertion, and implement a suitable Content Security Policy.

title: Stored XSS Through User Profile Data
impact: If malicious content is stored and later rendered without proper sanitization, JavaScript could execute when another user views the affected page.
remediation: Validate user data on the server, encode stored values when displaying them, avoid unsafe HTML rendering, and implement a suitable Content Security Policy.
